improvements: I-30 (order 28): re-derived assurance evidence -- the round's own guard mutations inside the pinned population, a runner whose kill names its test, and pinned helper modules
problems_addressed: R-66 (the audit's finding 91), the population half only; the freeze record half is batch 56 with the V4 verifier that reads it
what_this_part_is: Fifty-four batches of this round each wrote a guard-mutation script under benchmarks/core_v4_false_confidence/audit/ and a log beside it. That is 563 mutations of real evidence -- and it sits OUTSIDE the area the certificate pins, is applied by runners nobody certifies, and is described only by logs a reader has to trust. R-67 says so in two halves: the batch guards are not in the population, and a runner that treats any non-zero exit as a kill credits a guard for a failure that has nothing to do with it. R-68 is the same defect one level down: the suites the certificate DOES pin import helper modules it does not, so 'N/N killed' is a statement about bytes the certificate never measured.

what_was_already_seen.finding 92 (R-67): None of the 44 batch guards is in MUTATIONS, and two recorded kills (B1j, B1k) no longer apply to the tree.
what_was_already_seen.finding 97 (R-67): The runners mutate the shared checkout in place and treat any non-zero exit as KILLED.
what_was_already_seen.finding 93 (R-68): hybrid_synthetic.py is imported by ten certified targets and is not pinned; the branch changed it by twelve lines without moving the certificate.
what_was_already_seen.finding 91 (R-66): A fabricated assurance record with green flags and a copied population sha passes every V2/V3 assurance check.

measured_before_any_rule_was_written.entries_that_no_longer_describe_the_tree: 27 as first measured; 25 moved entries plus the 2 never-applied placeholders -- see amendment 1

the_rounds_guard_mutations_are_declared_.rule: `tests/mutation_population_v4.py` declares all 563 entries as DATA, one 9-tuple each: `(id, spec, old, new, target_test, expect, note, also, source)`. It is generated by `benchmarks/core_v4_false_confidence/audit/fold_v4_population.py`, which PARSES every batch script with `ast` rather than importing it, and it is committed inside the area the certificate pins.
the_rounds_guard_mutations_are_declared_.why: The number 563 is a count of what the round wrote, not a chosen threshold: the generator refuses to write if any entry cannot be read, so the count is the corpus and nothing is dropped silently. Parsing rather than importing is forced -- the batch 1-5 scripts run their mutations at import and one still names an absolute path from the machine the round started on.
the_rounds_guard_mutations_are_declared_.compatibility: Additive: a new test module and a new generator. No frozen symbol is touched.
the_rounds_guard_mutations_are_declared_.residual: The batch scripts stay where they are. They are the historical record of how each batch ran; the population is what is verified from now on.

every_folded_mutation_must_still_match_t.rule: A new FAST-tier suite, `tests/test_mutation_population_v4.py`, applies every entry (and every edit in its `also`) to the live source IN MEMORY: each must match exactly once inside its declared scope, and each must move `mutation_guards._code_digest`. The generator refuses to write a population that fails either check.
every_folded_mutation_must_still_match_t.why: This is the check `tests/test_mutation_harness.py` already makes for MUTATIONS, and the reason it exists: five pinned mutations had silently stopped applying and were reported as verified for months. Folding 563 unverified entries into the certified area without it would multiply that defect by twelve.
every_folded_mutation_must_still_match_t.residual: Matching exactly once is not a kill. Only the formal round establishes that, and it is the next rule.

a_kill_requires_the_named_target_test_to.rule: `tools/certification/mutation_v4_runner.py` runs each mutation in an ISOLATED copy of the tree, runs ONLY the entry's `target_test`, and writes JUnit XML. The verdict is KILLED only when that XML carries a `<testcase>` for the named nodeid with a `<failure>` in it. A collection error, an import error, a non-test exit code, an empty run, or a failure under any other nodeid is NOT a kill and is reported by name. The runner refuses to work in the repository itself.
a_kill_requires_the_named_target_test_to.why: Finding 97 exactly: a non-zero exit is not evidence about the guard the mutation names. The JUnit route is chosen over reading the terminal summary because the nodeid is IN the XML -- the summary line proves a failure happened, not whose.
a_kill_requires_the_named_target_test_to.compatibility: Additive: a new module in the already-pinned certification control plane.
a_kill_requires_the_named_target_test_to.residual: A target test that is itself broken at the measured commit would report a kill for the wrong reason. That is what the unmutated control run is for, and the runner refuses a round whose control is not green.

an_entry_whose_target_moved_is_repointed.rule: The 25 entries whose target moved (27 as first measured; see amendment 1) after the batch that wrote them are repointed in `REPOINTED` in the generator, each carrying the reason, the spec and text it used to name, and what it names now. The two entries a batch declared NOT MUTATED (a JSON edit, which breaks the parse; a prose edit, which changes no code) are marked `NOT_MUTATED` and are never applied. Entries a batch declared `SURVIVED` keep that expectation and their recorded reason.
an_entry_whose_target_moved_is_repointed.why: A stale mutation is a guard verified by nobody, which is the defect, and DELETING one is how that becomes invisible. Every rule these 27 name is still in the tree, so each can be repointed honestly. This includes B1j and B1k, which finding 92 names as no longer applying: the mission's final round expected them to be dropped, and both rules -- the supplied grid's goodness of fit and its containment -- are still there, one line each in the router's disjunction, so they are repointed instead. Dropping a live guard to match an expectation would be the weakening this round exists to remove.
an_entry_whose_target_moved_is_repointed.residual: Five entries change executable tokens only on Python 3.12+ (PEP 701: before it, an f-string was one dropped STRING token). Each mutates a refusal MESSAGE into the text the audit found misleading and is killed by a test that reads the message. They are declared in `FSTRING_ONLY_ON_3_12` and the suite asserts the set is exactly those five, so it cannot grow silently.

the_certificate_pins_every_module_its_ce.rule: `tools/certification/core_certificate.py` gains `harness_import_closure(root)`: the transitive closure, over `ast`-parsed imports, of every tests/-local module reachable from the mutation harness TARGETS and from every `target_test` the V4 population names. `scope_problems` refuses a scope whose harness area does not contain all of it. The harness area's patterns are extended to the closure (121 files).
the_certificate_pins_every_module_its_ce.why: Finding 93 is that the list was hand-maintained, so the fix cannot be a longer list. The closure is DERIVED and checked, which is what makes a helper added next year a failure rather than a silent gap.
the_certificate_pins_every_module_its_ce.compatibility: The harness area's digest moves, so `tests/test_core_certificate.py` and the freeze manifests fail until the V4 round regenerates them. Those suites are in the round's by-design failing set for exactly this reason.
the_certificate_pins_every_module_its_ce.residual: The closure follows STATIC imports. A helper reached only through `importlib` by a computed name would not be found; nothing in the closure does that, and the check reports what it measured.

the_population_digests_are_re_derived_fr.rule: `tools/certification/mutation_population.py` gains the V4 population beside the V1-V3 one: `v4_population(root)` reads `tests/mutation_population_v4.py`, computes `population_sha256` over the ordered ids and `definitions_sha256` over the canonical JSON of the full entries, and `v4_log_problems` re-derives each shard's verdicts from the runner's own transcript. A record's own digests are never trusted to describe the population they were checked against.
the_population_digests_are_re_derived_fr.why: Finding 91 is that a copied population sha passes. A digest that is recomputed from the tree and compared cannot be copied into a record; and `definitions_sha256` over the bodies means the same ids with a different mutation are a different population.
the_population_digests_are_re_derived_fr.compatibility: Additive: new functions beside the existing ones. `EXPECTED_FORMAL_POPULATION` (284) and the V1-V3 rules are untouched.
the_population_digests_are_re_derived_fr.residual: The freeze record half of R-66 -- re-deriving the measured commit and the figures a certificate asserts -- is batch 56, where the V4 verifier that reads the record is written. Recorded here so the split is a decision and not an omission.

the_formal_round_runs_in_four_shards_and.rule: The V4 population is run in `SHARD_COUNT = 4` shards under the existing rule `position % count == index`, and coverage is proved by membership (union is the population, pairwise disjoint, nothing unknown ran, every selected entry reached its declared verdict) rather than by a count.
the_formal_round_runs_in_four_shards_and.why: Four is a convention carried unchanged from the V1-V3 population: it is what the recertify workflow's matrix runs and it is the number the existing sharding proof is written for. It is a scheduling choice and no result depends on it -- the membership proof is what makes the round evidence.
the_formal_round_runs_in_four_shards_and.residual: 563 mutations, each a tree copy and one test, is hours of wall clock. The shard rule is what makes that a parallel round rather than a single one.

population_count.note: the corpus, counted by the generator; 563 of batches 1-54 plus batch 55's own 12 -- see amendment 2

repointed_entries.note: 25 repointed at their source and one (B17f) at its renamed target test; amended from 27, see amendments 1 and 3

fstring_only_on_3_12.note: asserted as an exact set, so it cannot grow silently

harness_closure_files.note: derived, then pinned; the check is the derivation

shard_count.note: convention carried from the V1-V3 population

compatibility: ADDITIVE ONLY. No V1-frozen symbol, default, field order or enum member is touched. The MCP verdict words are untouched. The certificate's harness area grows, which moves its digest and is settled by the V4 round in batch 56.
reproductions_first: Every rule above is recorded as a strict xfail in tests/test_core_scientific_audit_batch55.py before any of it is implemented, each seen failing ON ITS OWN ASSERTION.

amendment_log.changes: `repointed_entries` 27 -> 25, and `entries_that_no_longer_describe_the_tree` is restated as 25 moved entries plus 2 never-applied placeholders.
amendment_log.numbers_that_forced_it: The first measurement counted 27 entries whose `old` text does not match the live tree exactly once. Two of those -- B25j and B27g -- carry an EMPTY `old` and `new`: their batch declared them NOT MUTATED (a JSON edit breaks the parse; a prose edit changes no code) and excluded them from its own run. `str.count('')` returns len(text) + 1, so an empty pattern 'matches' 138459 times in certification/guard_reach_ledger.json and 103528 times in src/engcore/scientific/consensus.py -- which is why they appeared in the stale list at all. Neither can be repointed, because neither names a mutation. The entries that genuinely moved and are repointed with their reasons are 25.
amendment_log.what_did_not_change: No rule, no threshold class, and no entry. The two placeholders are carried with their batch's reason and marked NOT_MUTATED so nothing applies them, exactly as rule 4 preregistered; only the two counts the rule quotes are corrected.

amendment_log.changes: `population_count` 563 -> 575 and `batch_scripts_folded` 55 -> 56: batch 55's own twelve guard mutations are folded into the population too.
amendment_log.numbers_that_forced_it: 563 was measured before this batch wrote its own guard script. Leaving it out would put the guards over the population's machinery -- the kill rule, the isolation refusal, the derived closure, the two digests -- exactly where R-67 found the other 563: in a benchmarks/ script nothing verifies. B55a-B55l are 12, so the population is 575 from 56 scripts. The generator's own self-check keeps them honest: it refuses to write if any entry no longer matches, which is what caught B55a after the kill rule was corrected.
amendment_log.what_did_not_change: No rule and no class. The count is a DECISION recorded in `EXPECTED_V4_POPULATION`, so it moves in the same change that folds a batch in, which is what this is.

amendment_log.changes: `repointed_entries` 25 -> 26: B17f is repointed at its target TEST, not its source.
amendment_log.numbers_that_forced_it: The formal round's first shards reported NOT_COLLECTED for B17f: its target test `test_r02_the_claim_names_the_prediction_domain_it_cannot_yet_show` had been RENAMED inside its own batch to `test_r02_the_claim_names_the_prediction_domain`. Four more entries (B11a, B11j, B11k, B13l) reported NOT_COLLECTED for a different reason: their target tests are PARAMETRIZED, and pytest reports each case as `name[case]`, which the first kill rule did not match. The rule now matches a parameter case of the named function -- one failing case is the kill, and an entry that names one case explicitly, as thirteen reach-ledger entries do, still matches only that case.
amendment_log.what_did_not_change: No mutation, no source rule, and no expectation. What changed is the nodeid a kill must carry, in one entry, and the rule's reading of a parametrized report. The FAST check now verifies the target FUNCTION exists and not only its file -- the check that would have caught B17f before a round ran.
